editorial.headline: Toy Retail Is Nationally Open but Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Retailers of toys, party equipment and toy drones can register across all stated scales nationally, but Bali’s permanent moratorium blocks PMA registration for this activity.
editorial.body:
**A foreign investor cannot register this retail activity in Bali today.** Nationally, it is open to PMA and permits foreign ownership up to 100%. Bali reaches a different result: it is blocked for PMA registration by the province’s island-wide, permanent moratorium. The recorded reason is specific. At the Besar scale, every scope is classed by OSS as Low or Medium-Low risk, placing this activity within the restriction applied in May 2026.

At heart, this is a focused retail activity for games, toys and party equipment. The catalogue is intentionally broad: dolls, marbles, bekel, congklak, scrabble, carrom, musical-instrument toys, toy cars, toy weapons, toy cooking implements and toy household furniture all sit within it. The same is true of party costumes, masks, party souvenirs—including make-up and joke articles—and magic equipment. Retail sale of toy drones is expressly included, giving the activity a contemporary edge alongside its more familiar play and celebration merchandise. The list moves from small playthings to more elaborate themed purchases, but its organising principle remains the sale of play and party goods.

Registration is open at every scale named in the record: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That breadth is significant, but it does not turn the classification into a catch-all retail label. The activity remains anchored to retail merchandise listed above: playthings, party articles and toy drones. For a founder preparing the business, the useful discipline is to make the retail offer intelligible in those terms, matching the registered activity to what will actually be sold. Those scale labels identify who may enter the activity nationally, while its merchandise identifies what the retail business is.

The contrast is therefore binary, not marginal. At national level, the PMA status is TERBUKA, with the stated maximum foreign ownership of 100% and the cited basis of Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In Bali, the stated status is BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO. The island-wide permanent rule blocks PMA where the recorded risk treatment is Low or Medium-Low; for this activity, the Besar-scale OSS assessment triggers that outcome. Full foreign ownership is a national possibility, but it does not provide a PMA registration path in Bali today.
